newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn conditions decline last week.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn conditions decline last week.

text.p: Corn conditions declined during the latest week and as of Sunday the crop was 59 percent good to excellent, below the 70 percent in that category the previous week, according to the Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.
Thirty-two percent of the corn crop was fair and nine percent was poor to very poor.
Seven percent of the corn acreage was silking, behind 12 percent a year ago and behind the 32 percent average.
Seventy percent of the soybean crop was good to excellent, the same as the previous week. Twenty-five percent of the crop was fair and five percent was poor to very poor.
Winter wheat harvest was 76 percent complete, above the 69 percent a year ago and equal to the five-year average for this date.

Topsoil moisture levels were 13 percent very short, 48 percent short, 38 percent adequate and one percent surplus. Subsoil moisture levels were six percent very short, 32 percent short, 61 percent adquate and one percent surplus.
Pasture conditions were two percent excellent, 37 percent good, 43 percent fair, 16 percent poor and two percent very poor.
